import polars as pl
import geopandas as gpd
from plotnine import *
Code 
# Main Indicator Dataset (HIV Youth Knowledge)
hiv_knowledge = pl.read_csv("/content/unicef_indicator_1_clean.csv")

# Complementary Dataset (HIV Youth Testing)
hiv_testing = pl.read_csv("/content/UNICEF_HIV_TEST.csv")
Code 
# Get the most recent year's HIV youth knowledge per country
latest_avg_knowledge = (
hiv_knowledge
    .filter(pl.col("year") == pl.col("year").max().over("alpha_3_code"))
    .group_by("alpha_3_code", "country")
    .agg(pl.col("obs_value_percentage").mean().alias("avg_hiv_knowledge"))
)

# Get the most recent year's HIV youth testing per country from the complementary file

latest_avg_testing = (
   hiv_testing
    .filter(pl.col("year") == pl.col("year").max().over("alpha_3_code"))
    .group_by("alpha_3_code")
    .agg(pl.col("obs_value_percent").mean().alias("avg_hiv_testing"))
)

# We join on alpha_3_code to link HIV youth knowledge with HIV youth testing data
combined_data = (
    latest_avg_knowledge
    .join(
      latest_avg_testing,
        on='alpha_3_code',
        how='left'
    )
)

# 1. Create a metadata dictionary for UNICEF regions
region_mapping = {
    "Sub-Saharan Africa": ["BDI", "BEN", "COG", "COM", "UGA", "NGA", "NAM", "ZAF", "KEN", "ETH", "TZA", "LSO", "MDG", "GAB", "GIN", "GMB", "GHA", "COD", "ZWE", "MWI", "MRI", "MRT", "RWA", "ZMB", "AGO", "MOZ", "BFA", "MLI", "SEN", "SLE", "STP", "SWZ", "TCD", "TGO", "SOM", "CIV", "CMR"],
    "South Asia": ["AFG", "BGD", "BTN", "IND", "MDV", "NPL", "PAK", "LKA"],
    "Middle East and North Africa": ["DZA", "BHR", "DJI", "EGY", "IRN", "IRQ", "JOR", "KWT", "LBN", "LBY", "MAR", "OMN", "QAT", "SAU", "SDN", "SYR", "TUN", "ARE", "YEM"],
    "Latin America and Caribbean": ["ARG", "BHS", "BRB", "BLZ", "BOL", "BRA", "CHL", "COL", "CRI", "CUB", "DOM", "ECU", "GUY", "SLV", "GTM", "HTI", "HND", "JAM", "MEX", "NIC", "PAN", "PRY", "PER", "URY", "VEN"],
    "East Asia and Pacific": ["AUS", "KHM", "CHN", "FJI", "IDN", "JPN", "KIR", "PRK", "KOR", "LAO", "MYS", "MHL", "FSM", "MNG", "MMR", "NRU", "NZL", "PLW", "PNG", "PHL", "WSM", "SGP", "SLB", "THA", "TLS", "TON", "TUV", "VUT", "VNM"],
    "Europe and Central Asia": ["ALB", "AND", "ARM", "AUT", "AZE", "BLR", "BEL", "BIH", "BGR", "HRV", "CYP", "CZE", "DNK", "EST", "FIN", "FRA", "GEO", "DEU", "GRC", "HUN", "ISL", "IRL", "ITA", "KAZ", "KGZ", "LVA", "LIE", "LTU", "LUX", "MLT", "MCO", "MNE", "NLD", "MKD", "NOR", "POL", "PRT", "MDA", "ROU", "RUS", "SMR", "SRB", "SVK", "SVN", "ESP", "SWE", "CHE", "TJK", "TUR", "TKM", "UKR", "GBR", "UZB"]
}

# 2. Flatten the dictionary into a list of tuples using list comprehension
metadata_rows = [(country, region) for region, countries in region_mapping.items() for country in countries]

# 3. Convert to a Polars DataFrame
region_mapping_df = pl.DataFrame(metadata_rows, schema=["alpha_3_code", "UNICEF_Region"], orient="row")

# 4. Join the region data with our previous combined data
hiv_knowledge_testing_data_final = combined_data.join(region_mapping_df, on="alpha_3_code", how="left")

# 5. Convert to pandas for plotnine
scatter_data_pd = hiv_knowledge_testing_data_final.to_pandas()

scatter_plot = (
    ggplot(scatter_data_pd, aes(x="avg_hiv_knowledge", y="avg_hiv_testing")) +
    geom_smooth(method="lm", color="#2c3e50", linetype="dashed", size=1, se=False) +
    geom_point(aes(fill="UNICEF_Region"), color="white", size=4, alpha=0.8, stroke=0.5) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels=lambda l: [f"{v:.0%}" for v in l]) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels=lambda l: [f"{v:.0%}" for v in l]) +
    scale_fill_brewer(type="qual", palette="Set2") +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(
        title="Knowledge Translates to Action: HIV Awareness vs. Testing",
        subtitle="Correlating overall youth data (15-24) across global regions",
        x="Comprehensive HIV Knowledge (%)",
        y="Tested for HIV in past 12 months (%)",
        fill="Region"
    ) +
    theme(
        figure_size=(9, 6),
        text=element_text(family="sans-serif"),
        legend_position="right",
        plot_title=element_text(weight="bold")
    )
)

# 3. Load world geometries from Natural Earth shapefile
world = gpd.read_file("https://public.opendatasoft.com/api/explore/v2.1/catalog/datasets/world-administrative-boundaries/exports/shp")

# 4. Merge with our data using ISO 3-letter codes
map_df = latest_avg_knowledge[['alpha_3_code', 'avg_hiv_knowledge']].to_pandas()
world_merged = world.merge(map_df, left_on="iso3", right_on="alpha_3_code", how="outer")
world = world[world.name != "Antarctica"]

# 4. Build the map with the custom gradient

world_map_red = (
    ggplot(world_merged)
    + geom_map(aes(fill="avg_hiv_knowledge"), color="black", size=0.1)
    + scale_fill_gradient(
        low="#fee5d9",
        high="#a50f15",
        na_value="lightgrey",
        labels=lambda l: [f"{v:.0%}" for v in l]
        )
    + theme_void()
    + labs(
        title="Youth HIV Knowledge Around the World",
        subtitle="Darker red indicates a higher percentage of comprehensive knowledge",
        fill="Knowledge %"
    )
    + theme(figure_size=(12, 6))
)

import polars as pl
from plotnine import *
import pandas as pd

# 1. Get the latest year per country for Knowledge
latest_know_sex = (
    hiv_knowledge
    .filter(pl.col("year") == pl.col("year").max().over("alpha_3_code"))
)

# 2. Join with our elegant metadata dictionary
mapped_know = latest_know_sex.join(region_mapping_df, on="alpha_3_code", how="inner")

# 3. Group by BOTH Region and Sex, then calculate the average percentage
region_sex_avg = (
    mapped_know
    .group_by("UNICEF_Region", "sex")
    .agg(pl.col("obs_value_percentage").mean().alias("avg_knowledge"))
)

# 4. Convert to pandas for plotting
bar_data_pd = region_sex_avg.to_pandas()

# Add a formatted label column for geom_text (still keeping it for potential future use or if user changes mind)
bar_data_pd['formatted_label'] = bar_data_pd['avg_knowledge'].apply(lambda x: f"{x:.0%}")

# Optional: Sort regions alphabetically for consistent order on the x-axis
bar_data_pd['UNICEF_Region'] = pd.Categorical(
    bar_data_pd['UNICEF_Region'],
    categories=sorted(bar_data_pd['UNICEF_Region'].unique()), # No reverse needed for vertical
    ordered=True
)

# Determine the x-intercepts for the vertical lines based on the number of unique regions
num_regions = len(bar_data_pd['UNICEF_Region'].unique())
# Lines will be placed at 0.5, 1.5, ..., num_regions - 1.5
vline_xintercepts = [i + 0.5 for i in range(num_regions - 1)]

# 5. Build the Grouped Bar Chart
bar_chart = (
    ggplot(bar_data_pd, aes(x="UNICEF_Region", y="avg_knowledge", fill="sex")) + # Swap x and y

    # The Bars: position="dodge" puts them side-by-side
    geom_col(position=position_dodge(width=0.8), width=0.7, alpha=0.9) +

    # Add vertical lines to separate regions
    geom_vline(xintercept=vline_xintercepts, linetype="dashed", color="gray", size=0.5) +

    # Set the Y-axis to scale from 0% to 100%
    scale_y_continuous(labels=lambda l: [f"{v:.0%}" for v in l], limits=(0, .4)) +

    # Custom color palette for Male/Female
    scale_fill_manual(values={"Female": "#FF9DA7", "Male": "#045AFC"}) +

    theme_minimal() +
    labs(
        title="Knowledge of HIV Prevention among Youth (15-24) by Sex and Region",
        subtitle="Comparing the latest available overall youth data",
        x="UNICEF Region", # Updated x-axis label
        y="Comprehensive HIV Knowledge (%)", # Updated y-axis label
        fill="Sex"
    ) +
    theme(
        figure_size=(12, 6), # Increased figure width
        text=element_text(family="sans-serif", color="#2c3e50"),
        plot_title=element_text(weight="bold", size=14, margin={'b': 10}),
        panel_grid_major_y=element_blank(), # Removes horizontal lines crossing the bars
        legend_position="top",
        axis_text_x=element_text(angle=0, hjust=0.5) # Rotate x-axis labels for readability
    )
)
